newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Clinton urges more private money for east Europe.
newsitem.headline: Clinton urges more private money for east Europe.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton said on Wednesday former communist states in eastern Europe needed more investment from private sources, following up on the billions of dollars already pumped in by the West.
"I think that most of what still needs to be done is accelerate the pace of private investment, and it's very different in different countries," he told reporters after an EU-U.S. summit.

Clinton was in The Hague for a twice-yearly summit with the European Union before taking part in celebrations for the 50th anniversary of the Marshall Plan, which transferred more than $12 billion in aid to Western Europe after World War Two.

A host of European leaders has gathered at the Dutch seat of government to commemorate the plan, proposed in 1947 by Secretary of State George Marshall, which is widely credited with jump-starting Europe's shattered post-war economy and blocking the eastward spread of Communism.

"In today's dollars the value of the Marshall Plan investments in Europe was about $88 billion, I think that's right. We have seen the international financial institutions commit about $50 billion already to the former Communist countries, plus about $45 billion in private investment," Clinton said.

He added that work needed to be done with individual countries in the former Communist bloc to see what sort of fresh action was necessary, stopping short of directly answering journalists' questions on whether the United States was considering a new Marshall Plan for eastern Europe.
"We can't simply say to those countries (in eastern Europe) 'We want you to be free democracies, we want you to have economic reform and good luck'," said Clinton.

"What I think we have to do is work with each country and look at what are the laws, have the laws been changed so that we can use private capital in these countries. What kinds of public investments...still need to be made before private investment can work for these countries," he said.
"If the question is do we need to do more I think the answer is yes, but then we have to look nation by nation at what specifically needs to be done and at what they still need to do," Clinton said.
European Commission president Jacques Santer told the news conference that the EU could make a valuable contribution by weloming eastern European countries into the 15 nation bloc.
The June EU summit in Amsterdam is expected to agree internal reforms paving the way to invite up to a dozen ex-communist states to join the Union over the next 10 years.
"(The EU's) most significant contribution will be to welcome central and eastern European countries as members," said Santer.

Clinton is due later on Wednesday to address representatives of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), which groups the United States and Canada with European nations, as part of the Marshall Plan celebrations.
